report: Post-antibiotic eight-month bloody mucoid diarrhea with positive fecal C. difficile PCR and colonoscopic erythema from ascending colon to rectum supports active antibiotic-associated C. difficile colitis in this immunosuppressed patient. Low CRP, normal albumin, and normal ileocecal valve argue against IBD or CLL-related colitis; positive PCR and mucosal inflammation make simple dysbiosis unlikely. Missing toxin A/B or GDH testing means PCR positivity cannot fully exclude colonization, but active C. difficile colitis remains the leading diagnosis.
